claims.text: Composition tuning with a neural-network model can predict the magnetic behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Composition tuning with a neural-network model can predict the magnetocaloric behavior of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
A neural-network-guided composition-tuning method can optimize non-equiatomic HEAs for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications.
Composition tuning affects atomic arrangement and elemental distribution in the alloys.
Machine-learning algorithms can predict magnetocaloric properties from composition.
The proposed tuning will increase the magnetocaloric effect, ΔS, by 20% relative to untuned non-equiatomic HEAs.
The applicable composition range is 0.1 to 0.9 for each elemental component.
Model accuracy and the complexity of composition–structure–property relationships create uncertainty in the prediction.
The hypothesis is falsified if the predicted increase in ΔS is less than 10% relative to the baseline.
